title: Automated Compliance for Financial Data Pipelines
business: A regional financial services firm managing sensitive customer data across multiple AWS accounts.
problem: Manual auditing of infrastructure changes leads to configuration drift, where unauthorized security group modifications or unencrypted storage volumes persist undetected, increasing the risk of data exposure.
solution: AWS Config provides continuous monitoring and recording of resource configurations. By implementing managed rules, the firm can automatically evaluate resource states against security policies, triggering alerts or remediation actions the moment a non-compliant change occurs.
steps: Enable AWS Config in the target region to start recording resource configuration changes.
Select and deploy managed rules that enforce encryption-at-rest for storage volumes.
Configure an Amazon SNS topic to receive notifications whenever a resource is marked as non-compliant.
Review the resource timeline in the AWS Config console to identify the specific IAM user who initiated the non-compliant change.
outcome: The firm achieves a continuous compliance posture where security teams receive near real-time visibility into configuration drift, allowing for rapid remediation without manual periodic audits.
limitation: AWS Config incurs costs based on the number of configuration items recorded and the number of rule evaluations performed; to check this, monitor the monthly billing dashboard for Config-specific line items.
